title: Ancient China
examples: What were the main dynasties in ancient China?
How did the Great Wall help China?
What goods traveled along the Silk Road?

explain.say: China was ruled by many different dynasties over time. A dynasty is a family that rules a country for a long time.

items: Qin Dynasty: Built early sections of the Great Wall.
Han Dynasty: Expanded trade along the Silk Road.
Tang Dynasty: Period of great cultural flowering.

draw.text: Dynasties rule China for long periods.

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the Great Wall of China. Look at the wall, the watchtower and the battlements. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
The Great Wall was a massive series of fortifications. It was built to protect Chinese states and empires.

draw.text: Great Wall: Protection for Chinese states.

explain.say: The Silk Road was an ancient network of trade routes. It connected China with the West for centuries.

draw.text: Silk Road: Trade between East and West.

explain.say: Silk was the most famous good traded. People wanted Chinese silk for its beauty and rarity.
The exchange of goods was not the only thing that happened. Ideas and diseases also traveled this way.

draw.text: Ideas and diseases traveled the routes.

explain.say: In modern life, we see this idea in global shipping. Think about container ships moving goods everywhere.

faq.q: Why is the Great Wall not one single wall?
faq.a: It is not one single wall because it was built by different dynasties over many centuries. Different rulers added sections as needed for protection.
asks: Was the Great Wall all built at once?
How long was the Great Wall really?

faq.q: What was the main purpose of the dynasties?
faq.a: The main purpose of dynasties was to provide a stable government structure. They established laws and maintained order across the land.
asks: What did a dynasty do for China?
How was China ruled in the past?

faq.q: Did people only trade silk on the Silk Road?
faq.a: No, people traded many things besides silk. They also traded spices, porcelain, and precious metals like gold.
asks: What else traveled on the Silk Road?
Was silk the only thing traded?

faq.q: How did the Silk Road affect culture?
faq.a: It allowed different cultures to mix and share ideas. For example, Buddhism traveled from India into China along these routes.
asks: Did the Silk Road spread religion?
What cultural things moved along the road?

faq.q: What is the difference between the Great Wall and the Silk Road?
faq.a: The Great Wall was a physical defensive structure built on land. The Silk Road was a network of trade paths that moved goods and people.
asks: Is the Wall for trade or defense?
What was the function of the two things?

facts: China was ruled by many powerful dynasties over its history.
The Great Wall was built primarily for defense against northern invaders.
The Silk Road connected China with civilizations in the Middle East and the Mediterranean.
Silk was a highly valued commodity that traveled along these ancient routes.

quiz.say: Ancient China was ruled by a succession of powerful ruling families called:
quiz.why: Dynasties are the names of ruling families that controlled China over long periods of time.

wrong.0: Empires describe a large area controlled by a ruler, but 'dynasty' specifically refers to the ruling family line.
wrong.1: Kingdoms are smaller political units, whereas dynasties describe the ruling family over a large region.
wrong.2: Civilizations are complex societies, not the ruling family structure itself.

quiz.say: The Great Wall was built mainly to protect against:
quiz.why: The wall's primary function was military defense against groups coming from the north.

wrong.0: Trade was managed by routes like the Silk Road, not by the wall itself.
wrong.2: Coastal defenses were handled by different structures, not the main Great Wall.
wrong.3: While it offered some protection, its main documented purpose was external defense.

quiz.say: Which route was most famous for trading silk from China to the West?
quiz.why: The Silk Road is the specific name given to the ancient network that carried Chinese silk westward.

wrong.1: While sea routes were used, the primary historical route associated with silk is the overland Silk Road.
wrong.2: Spice routes focused mainly on spices, although they overlapped with the Silk Road.
wrong.3: River trade was important locally, but it did not represent the vast international network of the Silk Road.
